newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen faces shareholder suit over bid.
newsitem.headline: Loewen faces shareholder suit over bid.

text.p: A shareholder in Loewen Group Inc filed a class action lawsuit against the funeral service company and its directors seeking to force the company to negotiate with bidder Service Corp International, court documents showed on Tuesday.
The case was launched by shareholder Jerry Krim in California Superior Court in Los Angeles last week.
The lawsuit "was brought...to enjoin breaches of fiduciary duty including the purchase of properties in Los Angeles which are intended to thwart any takeover of the company," the action said.

Loewen has rejected a US$43 a share bid from Service, the biggest operator of funeral homes and cemeteries in North America. Service is widely expected to launch a formal hostile offer of up to US$48 a share after its board meets Tuesday.

The class action alleged that Loewen and its directors "improperly responded" to Service's bid by rejecting the offer, refusing to negotiate and paying an "inflated price of US$240 million" for the Rose Hills cemetery in Los Angeles. It alleged that the defandants were seeking to "thwart legitimate attempts to acquire the company" and entrench themselves, thereby breaching their fiduciary duty.

The action asked the court to order Loewen and its directors to "cooperate fully" with Service or anyone else who proposed a takeover of the company or other transaction that would maximize shareholder value.

It also sought to compel Loewen to create an "active auction" for the company, enjoin the implementation of its shareholder rights plan and bar completion of the Rose Hills deal and other extraordinary corporate transactions.
A Loewen spokesman was not immediately available for comment. A lawyer involved in the case said the defendants had not yet been served with the action.

Loewen faced similar lawsuits in the past. A shareholder class action suit was launched against the company last year in Mississippi after a jury there ordered the company to pay US$500 million in a breach-of-contract case. The action alleged that Loewen concealed its financial problems.
Loewen later settled the Mississippi lawsuit out of court for US$135 million in cash and stock. The fate of that class action was unclear.
